comments.author: @BrentDuty
comments.text:
The ancestry call of Cayman is strong. What most people outside of Cayman don’t realize is, most of us are related either by distant blood lines or by marriage. Our families, no matter the color share deep connections to one another and make up the fabric of true Caymanian culture, history, traditions. Quiet humility and respect is a source of currency among true Caymanians. When the sea bears down on an island so small, it becomes a ship. The true nature of this unit comes alive, the Caymanians don’t waiver, they show their ancestral instincts. Cayman is a place of risk takers inventive thinkers, skilled and brave. 

Don’t get me started on how the women were always the stronger half. The men picked women that could do it all on their own, because our fathers didn’t always come back and were taken by the sea. They were often left with a large family and they had to help one another and they often did. 

Cayman(kay-man) Caymanian (Kay-man-yen). Some of the most friendly beautiful people you’ll ever meet. You’ll know one once you speak to one, don’t let the tough face fool you. There’s gold in their hearts.

comments.author: @Sherpa8034
comments.text:
I first visited Grand Cayman over 55 years ago, and since then I have visited around 30 times or so. These islands have come a long way. Back then the population was somewhere between 12K and 14K. I remember days when George Town had far less building structures, and of those structures, many were only made of board. Walking the streets outside George Town, you could hear a pin drop because of how quiet the streets were in broad daylight. There was one bus - and yes, I said one bus - that ran the route from West Bay to George Town and from George Town to Bodden Town. If you missed the bus in West Bay, you had over an hour of wait for its return. 

There were only a few hotels along the Seven Miles Beach stretch of road. The heart of George Town had a mixture of dwelling board houses as well as commercial buildings made of board or concrete or both. Today, most residential dwellings are outside the of the town limits. Back then, water for home use came from wells and pumped into the pipelines in the houses. It was a simple yet one of the most peaceful settings you could find. My brother and his Caymanian wife who lived in West Bay at the time, gave rise to my extended Caymanian family, which is quite large today. Hence the reason I visit so often - as recently as last year. The thing I found most beautiful about Caymanians back then, was how friendly and respectful they were. A Caymanian would never pass you on the street without saying good day. They would greet you as if they had known you for many years. Is it so today? I cannot tell because there has been a massive influx of foreigners who live there now. Notwithstanding that, the Cayman Islands are among the top 5 places in the world I wouldn't think twice about living there.
